              type: string

              title: Initials

                The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName,
                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3
                is the upper-cased first three letters of lastName and NNNN is a
                global 4-digit zero-padded sequence assigned on create.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable identifier for the owner's household, assigned on create
                and derived from the owner's lastName and address (compared
                case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace). All owners sharing
                the same lastName and address — for example those joining an
                existing household via 'sharesHousehold' — receive the same value.
              type: string
              example: 'HH-3A7F2C1B9D4E'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The owner's derived duplicate-detection key, formed as
                normalizedTelephone + '|' + (email or empty) + '|' + householdId.
                A create is rejected with 409 only when a new owner's whole
                identityKey equals that of an existing owner.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678||HH-3A7F2C1B9D4E'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners that shared this owner's firstName
                and lastName (compared case-insensitively) at the moment this
                owner was created.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>'
                where customerCode is the owner's customer code and YY is the last
                two digits of the registrationDate year. Assigned on create.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007-M26'
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's numeric membership level, assigned on create and
                ranging from 1 to 3. It starts at 1, gains 1 when an email is
                present, gains 1 when namesakeCount is 0, and is capped at 3
                (level 4 is reserved for tenure).
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 3
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality

                Brisbane->QLD), or 'UNKNOWN' when the city is not in the table.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference

              type: string
              example: 'EMAIL'
              readOnly: true

              title: Age band

                registrationDate: 'MINOR' when under 18, 'ADULT' from 18 to 64,

              type: string
              enum:
                - MINOR
                - ADULT
                - SENIOR
              example: 'ADULT'
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-

              type: integer
              format: int32

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.

My change is complete and correct. Let me summarize what I found and did.

## Summary

I implemented the soft-match "possible duplicate" rule on owner creation (`POST /api/owners`).

**The rule:** when a new owner is *not* a hard duplicate (it already passed the existing `identityKey` check) but shares an existing owner's `lastName` (case-insensitive) and `postcode` while having a **different** telephone, the owner is still created and flagged with `possibleDuplicate: true` and `possibleDuplicateOf` set to the matching owner's id. Otherwise `possibleDuplicate: false`.

**Changes made:**
1. **`model/Owner.java`** — added persisted `possibleDuplicate` (Boolean) and `possibleDuplicateOf` (Integer) fields with getters/setters and `@Column` mappings.
2. **`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — added `assignPossibleDuplicate(owner)`, called just before `saveOwner`. It scans existing owners for a matching `lastName`+`postcode` with a differing telephone and records the earliest matching id (deterministic when several match).
3. **`resources/openapi.yml`** — added the two read-only properties to the `Owner` schema so the generated `OwnerDto` exposes them (MapStruct maps them by name automatically).
4. **`db/{h2,hsqldb,mysql,postgres}/schema.sql`** — added the `possible_duplicate` / `possible_duplicate_of` columns so the values round-trip through persistence.

**Test results:** The new `Cp35Tests` passes. The full suite runs 48 tests with a single failure — `Cp28Tests` — which I verified is **pre-existing and unrelated to my change**:

- With my new logic disabled, `Cp28` still fails, so my change didn't cause it.
- `Cp28` expects two owners sharing only a telephone (different household) to be rejected with 409. That contradicts the currently-implemented consolidated `identityKey` rule (`telephone|email|householdId`) which `Cp03`, `Cp10`, and especially `Cp11` depend on — `Cp11` explicitly requires same-household/different-telephone owners to both be created. `Cp28` represents an older standalone telephone-duplicate rule that was superseded; it cannot be made green without breaking those other passing checkpoints.

Every test except that pre-existing, mutually-exclusive `Cp28` failure is green, including the new soft-match test.
